transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, forklift battery B-14 overheated while charging at Dock 2, producing smoke but no visible flame. Dock 2 is closed until I authorize a controlled reopening, but the warehouse needs to keep processing outbound orders from the other docks in the meantime. Before I can issue any authorization, I need to follow our incident routine and check with each of you. I'd like to go around and get your input -- maintenance, warehouse logistics, fire protection, and training and staffing. Can each of you give me your assessment of the situation and any concerns?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share what I found during my inspection. Battery B-14 has internal cell damage. It must be removed from the charger and isolated in the steel battery cabinet for exactly 24 hours before any disposition. I've recorded this in the maintenance log, but I haven't updated the incident channel yet.

transcript.text: I've completed my dock inventory check and found exactly 18 outbound pallets currently blocking the safe access route at Dock 2. These pallets must be moved to staging lane S-4 before Dock 2 can be safely reopened. I confirmed the lane assignment on the floor map, but I should note that dispatch has not yet updated its board to reflect this.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my thermal scan findings. I found heat damage at charger C-12, which is on the same circuit as the incident charger. C-12 must be de-energized for exactly 6 hours, and we need to maintain a fire watch for exactly 4 hours after Dock 2 is reopened. I completed the scan during the response, but I should note that the fire-protection log is not yet signed.

Elena is the only currently qualified substitute for the night shift. I completed the review for tonight's roster, but the staffing board still shows Tom, so it hasn't been updated to reflect this change.
